title: The Hierarchy of Evidence and Where It Misleads

hook.en: Systematic reviews at the top, expert opinion at the bottom: a tidy pyramid. Useful, but a bad trial can sit above a good cohort study, and a randomised trial cannot tell you what harm looks like in the real world. Learn the pyramid, and learn where it lies.
hook.ur: Oopar systematic reviews, neeche expert ki raye: saaf pyramid. Mufeed hai, lekin kharab trial achhe cohort study se oopar baith sakta hai, aur randomised trial nahi bata sakta ke haqeeqi duniya mein nuqsan kaisa dikhta hai. Pyramid seekhein, aur yeh bhi ke yeh kahan jhoot bolta hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll place study designs on the evidence pyramid, explain why higher is usually but not always better, name when lower designs are the right choice, and describe how GRADE rates the certainty of evidence.
goal.ur: End tak aap study designs ko evidence pyramid par rakhenge, samjhayenge ke oopar hona aam taur par lekin hamesha behtar nahi, batayenge ke kab neeche ke designs sahi hain, aur GRADE evidence ki yaqeeniyat kaise rate karta hai.

text.en: The **hierarchy of evidence** ranks designs by how well they protect against bias when asking about treatment effects: systematic reviews of randomised trials, then randomised trials, cohort studies, case-control studies, case series and finally expert opinion. The ranking is a **starting point**. A well-run cohort study can beat a poorly run trial, and different questions (harm, prognosis, experience) need different designs at the top.
text.ur: **Evidence ka hierarchy** designs ko is bunyad par rank karta hai ke ilaaj ke asar ke sawal mein woh bias se kitna bachate hain: randomised trials ke systematic reviews, phir randomised trials, cohort studies, case-control studies, case series aur aakhir mein expert ki raye. Yeh ranking **aaghaz** hai. Achhi tarah chalaya gaya cohort study kharab trial ko mat de sakta hai, aur mukhtalif sawalon (harm, prognosis, tajurba) ko oopar mukhtalif designs chahiye.

text.en: Think of **witnesses in a court**. An eyewitness who saw the event is strong. A group of independent witnesses who agree is stronger. A rumour is weak. But an eyewitness who was drunk, far away or paid is not reliable, whatever their rank. Rank gives a first impression, and quality decides how much weight to give.
text.ur: **Adalat mein gawahon** ko sochein. Jis ne waqia dekha woh mazboot gawah hai. Kai azaad gawah jo mutafiq hon un se bhi mazboot. Afwah kamzor hai. Lekin nashe mein, door se dekhne wala ya paisa pane wala gawah bharosemand nahi, chahe uska rank kuch bhi ho. Rank pehla taassur deta hai, aur quality tay karti hai kitna wazan dein.

title.en: The evidence pyramid, and a limit for each level
title.ur: Evidence pyramid, aur har satah ki ek had

rows.en: Pools many trials and shows the overall picture
rows.ur: Kai trials jama kar ke kul tasveer dikhata hai

rows.en: Only as good as the trials inside it, and can be out of date
rows.ur: Utna hi achha jitne is ke andar ke trials, aur purana ho sakta hai

rows.en: Fair comparison, controls for known and unknown confounders
rows.ur: Munsifana muqabla, maloom aur na-maloom confounders ko control karta hai

rows.en: Often short, small, in selected patients, and poor at rare harms
rows.ur: Aksar mukhtasar, chhota, chunindah mareezon mein, aur nadir nuqsan mein kamzor

rows.en: Follows real people over time, good for prognosis and harms
rows.ur: Haqeeqi logon ko waqt ke saath follow karta hai, prognosis aur nuqsan ke liye achha

rows.en: Confounding: groups may differ in ways the study did not measure
rows.ur: Confounding: groups aise tareeqon se mukhtalif ho sakte hain jo study ne nahi naape

rows.en: Relies on memory and the choice of controls
rows.ur: Yaadasht aur controls ke intikhab par munhasir

rows.en: Describe new or rare events and spark ideas
rows.ur: Naye ya nadir waqiyaat bayan karte hain aur khayalat jagate hain

rows.en: No comparison, so no proof of cause
rows.ur: Muqabla nahi, isliye wajah ka saboot nahi
Jab kuch aur na ho tab mufeed

rows.en: Can be wrong, and affected by habit and authority
rows.ur: Ghalat ho sakti hai, aur aadat aur ikhtiyar se mutasir

question.en: You want to know how common serious side effects are after a technique in everyday practice, including rare ones. Which design is usually most informative?
question.ur: Aap jaanna chahte hain ke roz-marra practice mein ek technique ke baad seriyas side effects kitne aam hain, nadir bhi shamil. Aam taur par kaun sa design zyada maloomati hai?

text.en: A large cohort or registry study, because trials are often too small and short to see rare harms
text.ur: Bara cohort ya registry study, kyunke trials aksar nadir nuqsan dekhne ke liye bohat chhote aur mukhtasar hote hain

feedback.en: Yes — for rare harms, large observational data often answer better than trials.
feedback.ur: Haan — nadir nuqsan ke liye bara observational data aksar trials se behtar jawab deta hai.

feedback.en: One case cannot give a rate.
feedback.ur: Ek case se sharah nahi milti.

text.en: The first randomised trial that tested the technique's benefit
text.ur: Pehla randomised trial jis ne technique ka faida aazmaya

feedback.en: It may not have been designed to find rare harm.
feedback.ur: Shayad nadir nuqsan dhoondhne ke liye design nahi kiya gaya.

question.en: A randomised trial in which half the patients dropped out and assessors knew the groups is compared with a well-run cohort study with the same question. What is the best statement?
question.ur: Ek randomised trial jis mein aadhe mareez chhor gaye aur assessors ko groups maloom thay, ka muqabla usi sawal wale achhe chalaye gaye cohort study se hota hai. Behtareen bayan kya hai?

text.en: A randomised trial is always better, whatever its quality
text.ur: Randomised trial hamesha behtar hai, quality kuch bhi ho

feedback.en: Poor conduct can undo the advantage.
feedback.ur: Kharab amal fayda khatam kar sakta hai.

text.en: Cohort studies are always better than trials
text.ur: Cohort studies hamesha trials se behtar hain

feedback.en: The cohort needs to be well designed too.
feedback.ur: Cohort ko bhi achha design hona chahiye.

text.en: The trial's high rank is lowered by its flaws; the better-run cohort may be more trustworthy for this question
text.ur: Trial ka unchha rank uski kharabiyon se kam ho jata hai; behtar chalaya cohort is sawal ke liye zyada bharosemand ho sakta hai

feedback.en: Yes — design rank is a starting point, and quality can lower or raise confidence.
feedback.ur: Haan — design ka rank aaghaz hai, aur quality yaqeen ko kam ya zyada kar sakti hai.

text.en: Rates how certain we are about an effect (high, moderate, low, very low), considering risk of bias, inconsistency, imprecision, indirectness and publication bias
text.ur: Rate karta hai ke asar ke baare mein hum kitne yaqeeni hain (high, moderate, low, very low), risk of bias, inconsistency, imprecision, indirectness aur publication bias ko dekhte hue

feedback.en: Yes — it starts at the design but lowers or raises certainty using these factors.
feedback.ur: Haan — design se shuru hota hai lekin in factors se yaqeeniyat ko kam ya zyada karta hai.

text.ur: Journals ko unki shohrat se rank karta hai

feedback.en: GRADE rates certainty of evidence, not journals.
feedback.ur: GRADE evidence ki yaqeeniyat rate karta hai, journals nahi.

text.ur: Sabit karta hai ke ilaaj kaam karta hai

feedback.ur: GRADE yaqeeniyat batata hai, saboot nahi.

text.en: **Using the pyramid as a scoreboard.** Saying "it is only an observational study, so ignore it" or "it is a randomised trial, so it must be right" is lazy thinking. Ask: does this design suit my question, was it done well, and do the results hold together with other evidence? Remember that no trial exists for many things we do, and that lack of a trial is not proof of no effect.
text.ur: **Pyramid ko scoreboard banana.** "Yeh sirf observational study hai, nazar-andaaz karo" ya "yeh randomised trial hai, isliye theek hoga" susti ki soch hai. Poochhein: kya yeh design mere sawal ke liye munasib hai, kya achhe tarah hua, aur kya nateeje doosre evidence ke saath mel khate hain? Yaad rakhein ke bohat si cheezon ke liye trial maujood nahi, aur trial ka na hona asar na hone ka saboot nahi.

text.en: **Say how sure you are.** For example: "The research on this is small and not very strong, so I would call it a reasonable thing to try, not a sure thing. If it does not help in a few weeks, we will change." Matching your confidence to the strength of the evidence is honest, and keeps patients from feeling misled.
text.ur: **Batayein aap kitne yaqeeni hain.** Misaal: "Is par research chhoti aur kamzor hai, isliye main ise aazmane ki munasib cheez kahunga, yaqeeni nahi. Agar chand haftoon mein faida na ho to hum badal denge." Apna yaqeen evidence ki mazbooti ke mutabiq rakhna imaandari hai, aur mareezon ko gumrah hone se bachata hai.

question.en: Can expert opinion ever be the right source?
question.ur: Kya expert ki raye kabhi sahi zariya ho sakti hai?

answer.en: Yes, when nothing better exists, for example for a rare condition, a new situation or an urgent decision. The risk is overconfidence, so a good expert says what they know, what they do not know and what the opinion is based on, and prefers a consensus of several experts to one voice.
answer.ur: Haan, jab behtar kuch maujood na ho, masalan nadir bimari, nayi surat-e-haal ya urgent faisle ke liye. Khatra zyada yaqeen hai, isliye achha expert batata hai ke woh kya jaanta hai, kya nahi jaanta aur raye kis par mabni hai, aur ek awaaz ke bajaye kai experts ke ittefaq ko tarjeeh deta hai.

beats.patient: A therapist asks whether a certain stretch is safe after a hip replacement. There are no trials, but several large registry studies and a surgeon consensus statement agree that it is safe if movement precautions are followed.
beats.assessment: There is no trial, but a body of observational data and expert consensus exists.
beats.treatment: She treats the evidence as moderate to low certainty, follows the consensus precautions and tells the patient what is known and unknown.
beats.reassess: The plan is safe and transparent, and she updates it when a trial appears.

text.en: **Absence of a trial is not proof of safety.** Many safe things were never tested, and so were many unsafe ones. When a treatment carries real risk, such as a high-velocity manipulation or a loading programme in a fragile patient, look for harm data specifically, and use caution when you cannot find it.
text.ur: **Trial ka na hona safety ka saboot nahi.** Bohat si mehfooz cheezein kabhi test nahi hui, aur bohat si ghair mehfooz bhi. Jab ilaaj mein haqeeqi khatra ho, jaise high-velocity manipulation ya kamzor mareez mein loading programme, to khaas taur par nuqsan ka data dhoondein, aur na milne par ehtiyat karein.

text.en: The "new evidence pyramid" proposed by Murad and colleagues redrew the classic pyramid with a wavy line between designs, to show that quality can move a study up or down, and placed systematic reviews as a lens through which to view other evidence, not just a top layer. The GRADE approach rates the certainty of a body of evidence, beginning with the design, and lowers it for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision and publication bias, and raises it for large effects and dose-response gradients.
text.ur: Murad aur saathiyon ke tajweez kiye "new evidence pyramid" ne classic pyramid ko designs ke beech lehradar lakeer se dobara banaya, yeh dikhane ke liye ke quality study ko oopar ya neeche kar sakti hai, aur systematic reviews ko doosre evidence dekhne ke ek lens ke taur par rakha, sirf sab se oopar ki tah nahi. GRADE ka tareeqa evidence ke majmoo'e ki yaqeeniyat ko rate karta hai, design se shuru hokar, aur risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision aur publication bias par kam karta hai, aur bade asar aur dose-response gradient par barhata hai.

text.en: **Rank, then Quality.** Use design as a first guess, then check how well it was done, and whether it fits your question.
text.ur: **Rank, phir Quality.** Design ko pehla andaaza samjhein, phir dekhein kitna achha hua, aur aap ke sawal se milta hai ya nahi.

summary.en: The pyramid is a starting point: systematic reviews and trials usually rank above observational studies, but quality and fit to the question matter more.
summary.ur: Pyramid aaghaz hai: systematic reviews aur trials aam taur par observational studies se oopar, lekin quality aur sawal se mutabiqat zyada ahem hain.

summary.en: Different questions need different designs: cohorts for prognosis and rare harms, qualitative studies for experience.
summary.ur: Mukhtalif sawalon ko mukhtalif designs chahiye: prognosis aur nadir nuqsan ke liye cohorts, tajurbe ke liye qualitative studies.

summary.en: GRADE rates certainty; "no trial" does not mean "no effect" and does not mean "safe".
summary.ur: GRADE yaqeeniyat rate karta hai; "trial nahi" ka matlab "asar nahi" aur "mehfooz" nahi.

front.en: What is at the top of the classic evidence pyramid for treatment questions?
front.ur: Ilaaj ke sawalon ke liye classic pyramid ke oopar kya hai?
Nadir nuqsan ke liye kaun sa design munasib hai?

back.en: The certainty of a body of evidence.

front.en: Can a cohort study beat a poor trial?
front.ur: Kya cohort study kharab trial ko mat de sakta hai?

back.en: Yes; quality matters as much as design.
back.ur: Haan; quality utni hi ahem hai jitna design.

note.en: Matching the question to the design.
